LESSON: APPROXI MATIONS AND ERRORS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: MEASUREMEN TS
Topic 3.6: Approxi mations and Errors
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Approxi mations and Errors, part of MEASUREMEN TS in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we estimate measurements of different quantities? 2. Why do we appreciate approximatio ns and errors in real life situations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Approxi mations and Errors together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Creativity and imagination: The learner undertakes group tasks and gains new perspectives on how to measure different

quantities such as length, area, volume, capacity and mass.

Values:
● Integrity: The learner enhances accountability as they measure different quantities and minimise errors.

● Responsibility: The learner enhances accountability as they take care of tools for measuring different quantities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Safety and security: The learner handles measuring tools with care.

Link to other subjects:

Integrated Science: The learner measures different quantities while carrying out experiments.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Digital devices with assistive technology such as screen readers, screen magnifiers and adapted keyboard, measuring

instruments such as meter rule, weighing scales, Print and Braille Course Book.
